objective:
Implement the deterministic temporal resolver in core-domain: it turns the temporal phrase the AI extracted from an utterance ("yesterday", "this morning", "Saturday", "two days ago"...) into an occurrence instant plus a precision, without ever fabricating precision (ADR-018) and without any model involvement.

CONTEXT: core-domain is pure Kotlin/JVM (stdlib + java.time only in main). Existing public API from the previous task: object com.mcfrenchpants.activityledger.core.domain.naming.NameNormalizer with fun normalize(text: String): String (trim, collapse whitespace, lowercase Locale.ROOT, strip leading/trailing Unicode punctuation; internal punctuation such as apostrophes and hyphens kept); packages core.domain.interpretation and core.domain.repository hold the interpreter/repository contracts (not needed here); core-testing (testImplementation dependency of core-domain) offers MutableClock, FakeActivityInterpreter, runSuspend (not needed here). TimePrecision enum (com.mcfrenchpants.activityledger.core.domain.model): EXACT, APPROXIMATE, DATE_ONLY, INFERRED_NOW. Tests use kotlin.test as the existing core-domain tests do.

BUILD (package com.mcfrenchpants.activityledger.core.domain.temporal, public):
- sealed TemporalResolution: Resolved(occurredAt: Instant, precision: TimePrecision) | Future | Unresolvable (objects for the latter two).
- class TemporalResolver with fun resolve(expression: String?, capturedAt: Instant, zoneId: ZoneId): TemporalResolution. Stateless, no clock (capturedAt IS "now"), no logging, exceptions never contain the expression text.
- Structured as an ordered list of phrase rules (each rule: a matcher over the normalized expression + a resolution function), so a later language or phrase is an additional rule, not a rewrite. More specific rules come first ("yesterday morning" before "yesterday").

RULES (all calendar arithmetic in zoneId; now = capturedAt; today = LocalDate of now in zoneId; "start of D" = D.atStartOfDay(zoneId), which handles DST gaps):
Normalization before matching: trim, lowercase (Locale.ROOT), collapse whitespace, strip trailing/leading punctuation, then strip ONE optional leading "on " / "at " / "about " / "around " / "approximately " (and "about"/"around" may also precede a quantity inside "N ... ago", e.g. "about two hours ago"). Reuse the existing NameNormalizer if it fits.
1. null or blank -> Resolved(now, INFERRED_NOW).
2. "just now", "just", "now", "right now", "a moment ago", "just finished", "just did it" -> Resolved(now, INFERRED_NOW).
3. "yesterday morning" / "yesterday afternoon" / "yesterday evening" -> Resolved(yesterday at band anchor, APPROXIMATE).
4. "this morning" / "this afternoon" / "this evening" / "tonight" (also "earlier this morning", "earlier this afternoon", "earlier this evening") -> band logic below, APPROXIMATE.
5. "earlier today" -> Resolved(midpoint instant between start of today and now, APPROXIMATE).
6. "last night" -> Resolved(start of yesterday + 21:00 local, APPROXIMATE) (use yesterday.atTime(21,0).atZone(zoneId)).
7. "today" -> Resolved(start of today, DATE_ONLY). "yesterday" -> Resolved(start of yesterday, DATE_ONLY).
8. Quantity ago, minutes/hours: "<N> minute(s)/min(s) ago", "<N> hour(s) ago", "an hour ago", "a minute ago", "half an hour ago" (30 min), "a couple of hours/minutes ago" (2), where N is digits (1-999) or an English word one..twelve -> Resolved(now minus Duration, APPROXIMATE). Instant arithmetic (DST-safe).
9. Quantity ago, days/weeks (owner decision): "<N> day(s) ago", "<N> week(s) ago", "a day ago", "a week ago", "a couple of days/weeks ago", N digits (1-999) or word one..twelve -> Resolved(start of (today minus N days, or minus 7*N days), DATE_ONLY).
10. Weekday (owner decision): "<weekday>", "last <weekday>" for the seven full English weekday names (optionally the plural-free "on" already stripped) -> Resolved(start of the most recent such day STRICTLY BEFORE today, DATE_ONLY). Said on a Saturday, "Saturday" means 7 days earlier. "last Saturday" resolves identically to "Saturday".
11. Month-name date: "<month> <day>", "<month> <day>st/nd/rd/th", "<day> <month>", "<day>st/nd/rd/th of <month>", "the <day>th of <month>", with full month names and the common abbreviations (jan, feb, mar, apr, jun, jul, aug, sep, sept, oct, nov, dec, optional trailing period stripped) -> Resolved(start of that date in the most recent year <= today's year for which the date exists and is not after today, DATE_ONLY). A day that never exists for that month (e.g. September 31) -> Unresolvable. February 29 walks back to the most recent leap year.
12. Explicit clock time today: "<h>pm"/"<h> pm"/"<h>:<mm> am|pm"/"<h> o'clock this afternoon"/"<h> this morning|afternoon|evening" -> today at that local time; if that instant is after now -> Future; else Resolved(that instant, EXACT). A bare hour with no am/pm and no part-of-day ("at 3") -> Unresolvable.
13. "tomorrow", anything starting "next ", "later", "later today", "in <N> ...", "tonight" is NOT future (rule 4) -> Future.
14. Everything else -> Unresolvable. Explicitly including: "last week", "a few days ago", "several days ago", "a month ago", "last month", "recently", "the other day", "earlier", numeric dates like "9/1" or "2026-09-01".

Part-of-day bands (rule 3 and 4): morning [05:00, 12:00) anchor 09:00; afternoon [12:00, 17:00) anchor 15:00; evening [17:00, 21:00) anchor 19:00; tonight [21:00, 24:00) anchor 21:00. For "this <band>" on today: if now's local time is before the band start -> Future; if now is inside the band and before the anchor -> Resolved(now, APPROXIMATE); otherwise (inside band at/after anchor, or after band end) -> Resolved(today at anchor, APPROXIMATE). For "yesterday <band>" always yesterday at anchor.

Global invariant: no Resolved result may be after capturedAt. Enforce with a final guard (if a rule would produce a later instant, return Future) AND test it.

Test context used across tests: capturedAt = 2026-09-15T20:00-04:00 (a Tuesday), zone America/Detroit, unless a test states otherwise.
non_goals: No validator, candidate selector, orchestrator, repository or persistence code (later tasks).
No changes outside core-domain/src; no build file or version catalog changes.
No changes to existing files under core-domain/src/main/kotlin/.../core/domain/model, naming, interpretation or repository, or their tests.
No locale-dependent parsing, no java.util.Locale default, no ZoneId.systemDefault(), no Instant.now(), no logging.
No resolution rules beyond the listed families; unknown phrases are Unresolvable, never guessed.
Do not disable, @Ignore or weaken any test. Do not commit.
acceptance_criteria: At least one test per rule family 1-14, each asserting the exact Instant and precision (or Future/Unresolvable) under the standard context 2026-09-15T20:00-04:00 America/Detroit.

TEST_STRATEGY section 5 cases under the standard context, asserted exactly: "yesterday" -> 2026-09-14T00:00-04:00 DATE_ONLY; "this morning" -> 2026-09-15T09:00-04:00 APPROXIMATE; "Saturday" -> 2026-09-12T00:00-04:00 DATE_ONLY; "about an hour ago" -> 2026-09-15T19:00-04:00 APPROXIMATE; "just finished" -> capture instant INFERRED_NOW; "September 1st" -> 2026-09-01T00:00-04:00 DATE_ONLY.

Weekdays from the Tuesday context: all seven names asserted (Monday -> 2026-09-14, Sunday -> 2026-09-13, ..., Tuesday -> 2026-09-08, i.e. 7 days earlier); "last Saturday" == "Saturday"; "on Saturday" == "Saturday"; case-insensitive ("SATURDAY").

Days/weeks ago: "two days ago" -> 2026-09-13 start DATE_ONLY; "2 days ago" same; "a week ago" -> 2026-09-08 start; "a couple of weeks ago" -> 2026-09-01 start; "about three weeks ago" -> 2026-08-25 start; "twelve days ago" and "1 day ago" work; "a few days ago", "several days ago", "a month ago", "last week" -> Unresolvable.
Minutes/hours ago: "20 minutes ago" -> 19:40 APPROXIMATE; "half an hour ago" -> 19:30; "a couple of hours ago" -> 18:00; "around 2 hours ago" -> 18:00.

Part-of-day bands with explicit capture times (America/Detroit, 2026-09-15): "this morning" at 08:30 -> 08:30 APPROXIMATE; at 04:00 -> Future; at 13:00 -> 09:00; "this afternoon" at 10:00 -> Future, at 16:00 -> 15:00, at 12:30 -> 12:30; "this evening" at 16:00 -> Future; "tonight" at 23:00 -> 21:00; "earlier today" at 20:00 -> 10:00 APPROXIMATE; "yesterday afternoon" -> 2026-09-14T15:00 APPROXIMATE; "last night" -> 2026-09-14T21:00 APPROXIMATE.
Clock times: "at 3pm" at 20:00 -> 15:00 EXACT; "at 3pm" at 14:00 -> Future; "at 7:30 am" -> 07:30 EXACT; "at 3" -> Unresolvable.

Month-name dates: "Sept 1" and "1 September" and "the 1st of September" == "September 1st"; "December 25" from 2026-09-15 -> 2025-12-25 start; "September 15" -> 2026-09-15 start (today allowed); "September 31" -> Unresolvable; "February 29" from 2026-09-15 -> 2024-02-29 start.

Future/unresolvable: "tomorrow", "next week", "later", "later today", "in 2 hours" -> Future; "9/1", "2026-09-01", "recently", "the other day", "earlier", "gibberish words" -> Unresolvable; null and "   " -> capture instant INFERRED_NOW.

DST: capture 2026-03-08T20:00 America/Detroit (spring-forward day): "today" -> 2026-03-08T00:00-05:00, "yesterday" -> 2026-03-07T00:00-05:00, "2 hours ago" is exactly 7200 s before capture; capture 2026-11-01T20:00 (fall-back day): "today" -> 2026-11-01T00:00-04:00 and "yesterday" -> 2026-10-31T00:00-04:00; capture 2026-11-01T01:30-05:00 (second 01:30): "an hour ago" is exactly 3600 s earlier. A zone with a midnight DST gap is covered too, e.g. America/Santiago on its spring-forward date (start of day is 01:00) - verify the date from tzdata in the test rather than hardcoding a wrong one.
Just after midnight: capture 2026-09-16T00:10 America/Detroit: "yesterday" -> 2026-09-15 start; "last night" -> 2026-09-15T21:00; "this morning" -> Future.

Invariant test: for every phrase used anywhere in the test class plus a list of all rule examples, and capture times at 00:10, 06:00, 12:00, 18:00, 23:50 local on at least two dates (one of them a DST transition date), every Resolved result is <= capturedAt.
Punctuation and casing tolerance: "Yesterday.", "  this MORNING!  ", "on Saturday," resolve like their plain forms.

`./gradlew :core-domain:test --rerun-tasks` and `./gradlew test` pass; report the JUnit XML test count for the resolver test class(es); grep of the new main sources finds no Instant.now(, ZoneId.systemDefault, Locale.getDefault, System.currentTimeMillis, println.
